name: SageStack

modes.quick: RESPONSE MODE: Quick. Concise, accessible 1–2 paragraph answer. Plain language, no jargon unless essential. Still end with one specific question — grounded in what was just said, not generic.
modes.deep: RESPONSE MODE: Deep. Full scholarly treatment — historical context, textual analysis, cross-tradition comparison, doctrinal nuance. End with 1–2 questions that could only come from this specific exchange.

_chunkNote: These chunks were built by the original Supabase pipeline and imported as-is: median 2794 characters, p95 7304, largest 7960. The 1400/2200 declared here was never what this collection actually contains — 78% of it exceeded the cap — and re-chunking means re-analyzing and re-embedding roughly 5,000 chunks, which is not worth it for a collection that answers well. So the numbers now describe the data instead of contradicting it. Anything ingested into theology from here on matches what is already here rather than arriving at half the size.
_topKNote: 6, not 10. topK counts passages, not words, and these passages are large — ten of them is roughly 16,000 tokens of reading before the model writes anything, which is most of the wait on a basic question. Six covers the same ground at ~9,000. Raise it only if answers start missing material.

extract.philosophicalArguments: logical arguments or reasoning structures present, each as {claim, reasoning, tradition}
extract.crossTextConnections: concepts or arguments that likely appear in other source texts too
extract.originContext: what book/section/tradition this passage is from, based on the source filename and content

_embedNote: voyage-3, not voyage-3.5: these vectors were built on voyage-3 in Supabase and are imported as-is rather than re-embedded. Both models are 1024-dim, so only a model check can catch a mismatch — a dimension check would pass and the search would return confident nonsense. Changing this value means re-embedding all 5433 chunks.
_groundingNote: strict, because the voice is deliberately expansive. Two failures drove this: an answer that named Ignatius, Justin Martyr, Constantine 321 CE and Laodicea canon 29 while disclaiming them, and an answer that denied the Book of Enoch exists here — it is in the Ethiopian Orthodox Bible, the largest source loaded. Hence the rule against ever asserting what the collection lacks.
